finding.reason: After SSE client disconnect, the server-owned provider/finalize task must continue. Therefore the inference slot plus conversation and turn-affinity locks must be owned by that server task, not by the client-facing generator. Releasing those locks while commit-critical work continues permits a second same-key request to overlap the first transaction.
finding.current_server_reference: The current stream run_request coroutine itself enters responses_inference_slot -> conversation_segments.lock -> turn_affinities.lock before handle_openai_responses; final Stage-B integration must preserve this ownership shape while replacing pre-commit protocol output with buffered durable projection.

checks: client waiter cancellation does not cancel server-owned transaction
conversation lock remains held while durable transaction is pending
turn-affinity lock remains held while durable transaction is pending
second same-key operation cannot enter before first finishes
negative control proves client-owned lock can be released while detached task still runs

integration_rule: Start one server-owned task whose coroutine itself acquires inference/conversation/affinity ownership and runs StageBTransactionCoordinator.execute. The SSE generator may shield/wait/project that task, but must not own those locks or cancel the task after provider work begins.
